text: Sing, barren woman, you who never bore a child; break into song and shout for joy, you who never went into labor. For the children of the desolate woman are more than the children of her who has a husband, says the LORD.
Enlarge the site of your tent, stretch out the curtains of your dwellings — do not hold back. Lengthen your ropes and drive your stakes deep.
For you will spread out to the right and to the left; your offspring will possess the nations and settle the desolate cities.
Do not be afraid, for you will not be put to shame; do not be dismayed, for you will not be disgraced. You will forget the shame of your youth and remember no more the reproach of your widowhood.

versions.text: Do not be afraid, for you will not be put to shame; do not be discouraged, for you will not be humiliated. You will forget the shame of your youth and remember no more the disgrace of your widowhood.
versions.explanation: תִּכָּלְמִי belongs to the semantic field of shame/humiliation rather than discouragement; "do not be dismayed" keeps the shame imagery of the verse intact while avoiding repetition of "humiliated" alongside "put to shame."

text: For your Maker is your husband — the LORD of hosts is his name — and your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel; he is called the God of all the earth.
The LORD has called you back like a wife deserted and grieved in spirit, like a wife married in youth only to be rejected, says your God.
For a brief moment I abandoned you, but with great compassion I will gather you back.
In a surge of anger I hid my face from you for a moment, but with everlasting love I will have compassion on you, says the LORD, your Redeemer.
For me this is like the waters of Noah: as I swore that the waters of Noah would never again cover the earth, so I have sworn not to be angry with you, never to rebuke you again.

versions.text: To me this is like the days of Noah, when I swore that the waters of Noah would never again flood the earth. So now I have sworn not to be angry with you, never to rebuke you again.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew text reads "the waters of Noah" (מֵי נֹחַ), not "the days of Noah." Rendering the first occurrence as "days" and the second as "waters" also creates an inconsistency within the same verse. Keeping "waters" both times preserves the imagery of the flood oath and the parallel structure ("as I swore… so I have sworn").

text: Though the mountains may depart and the hills be shaken, my steadfast love will not depart from you, nor will my covenant of peace be shaken, says the LORD, who has compassion on you.
Afflicted city, storm-tossed and uncomforted, I will set your stones in antimony and lay your foundations with sapphires.
I will make your battlements of rubies, your gates of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious stones.
All your children will be taught by the LORD, and great will be their peace.
You will be established in righteousness. Oppression will be far from you — you will have nothing to fear; terror will be far removed — it will not come near you.
If anyone attacks you, it will not be from me; whoever attacks you will fall before you.
See, it is I who created the blacksmith who fans the coals into flame and forges a weapon fit for its work; and it is I who created the destroyer to wreak havoc.

No weapon forged against you will succeed, and you will refute every tongue that rises against you in judgment. This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, and their vindication from me, declares the LORD.
